name: names for the Otherworld

attributes.attribute: many evocative names for the Celtic paradise
fairy queen of a floating island

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: No taboo barred naming the Otherworld, as there was with the fairies. Yet many evocative names describe the Celtic paradise. Ildathach means many-colored land. Mag Mór is the great plain, while Mag Mell is the honey plain. Mag Mon is the sports plain, Mag Réin the sea plain. Further names include Tir na nÓg, the land of the young; Tir na mBan, a land of the women; and Tir Tairngiri, the promised land. Some names mark a specific realm, such as the floating island of the fairy queen Niamh. More often they are interchangeable.

okr.objective: names for the Otherworld evoke the Celtic paradise.
